events.region: Eastern Black Range Foothills; Sierra County Lakes; Southern Gila Region Highlands/Black Range
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 330 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 5
miles southwest of San Miguel, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Cuchillo, Truth or Consequences, San Miguel, City of Elephant Butte,
Palomas, Williamsburg, Elephant Butte Lake, Upper Palomas Canyon,
Lost Canyon, Lower Palomas Canyon, Ash Canyon, Rock Canyon, Hot
Springs Landing, Lakeshore Highlands, and Lions Beach.

This includes Interstate 25 in New Mexico between mile markers 67 and
81.

events.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to
10 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip
currents.

* WHERE...For the High Surf Advisory the most vulnerable areas for
high surf and beach erosion include Pinones along Road 187,
Parcelas Suarez, Villas del Mar, and Villa Christiana in Loiza;
Fortuna in Luquillo; Pueblo and Tamarindo in Aguadilla; Barrio
Obrero, Pueblo and Jareaito in Arecibo; Las Boca in Barceloneta;
Machuca in Manati; Puerto Nuevo in Vega Baja; Ocean Park in San
Juan; and Barrio Espinal in Aguada. For High Rip Current Risk,
the most vulnerable areas are the exposed northwesterly and
north- facing beaches. For the High Rip Current Risk, the most
vulnerable areas are the exposed northwesterly and north-facing
beaches. Breaking waves can continue to reach 7 to 9 feet
tonight.

* WHEN...The High Surf Advisory remains until 6 PM AST this
evening. The High Rip Current Risk remains through Wednesday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...For the High Surf Advisory, high waves that can wash
over jetties and sweep people and pets onto jagged rocks. Rough
surf may also knock you down. Large breaking waves will result
in localized beach/dune structure erosion and dangerous swimming
conditions. For the High Rip Current Risk, rip currents can
sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water,
where it becomes difficult to return to safety.

events.region: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island; Interior Kuskokwim Delta; Northern Bristol Bay Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...South to southeast winds 35 to 50 mph with gusts up to 70
mph possible.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, and Northern Bristol Bay Coast.

* WHEN...From Friday morning through Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong, storm force Bering front is on track
to sweep the Aleutian Chain and arrive to the Kuskokwim Delta/coast
and Bristol Bay coast Friday morning. There is currently medium to
high confidence (60 to 80 percent chance) of wind gusts exceeding
60 mph for these locations.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 40 to 50 mph with gusts up to 75 mph
possible.

* WHERE...Aleutians East Borough, including Cold Bay and King Cove.

* WHEN...From Friday morning through Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A storm force Bering front will bring strong
southeast winds to Cold Bay and King Cove. As winds are enhanced
through the southeast to northwest oriented gap, there is medium
confidence (40 to 60 percent chance) of wind gusts reaching 75 mph
or greater.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Multiple periods of heavy rain are expected for the Icy Strait
corridor and northeast Gulf Coast, including the following
communities: Yakutat, Elfin Cove, Pelican, Gustavus, Juneau. Elevated
gusty winds are expected alongside this heavier rainfall, with the
strongest winds from the southwest expected late this morning into
this afternoon. Prolonged periods of moderate to heavy rain will
produce significant river rises with the potential for at least minor
flooding in Juneau and Gustavus. Ponding of water in low-lying areas
is also possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Eastern Gulf Coast and Northeast Gulf
Coast. This includes the cities of Elfin Cove And Pelican.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals for the Elfin Cove and Pelican area through this
evening range between 3-4 inches, with greater than 6 inches
possible at elevations greater than 1000 ft. Coinciding with high
rain rates, possibly exceeding 0.3 inches per hour, elevated wind
gusts greater than 40 mph are expected at elevations greater than
500 ft.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Glacier Bay; City and Borough of Juneau
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Multiple periods of heavy rain are expected for the Icy Strait
corridor and northeast Gulf Coast, including the following
communities: Yakutat, Elfin Cove, Pelican, Gustavus, Juneau. Elevated
gusty winds are expected alongside this heavier rainfall, with the
strongest winds from the southwest expected late this morning into
this afternoon. Prolonged periods of moderate to heavy rain will
produce significant river rises with the potential for at least minor
flooding in Juneau and Gustavus. Ponding of water in low-lying areas
is also possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Northern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Gustavus And Juneau.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded. Isolated landslides are
possible in areas of steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals ranging between 1.5-2.5 inches, exceeding 4 inches on
south to southwest facing mountains along the outer coast, and
exceeding 4 inches on south to southwest facing mountains at
elevation in Glacier Bay and around Gustavus.

For the Juneau area, rain totals have trended slightly down,
ranging between 2 and 3 inches with totals exceeding 4 inches at
elevations greater than 4 inches. Highest rain rates are expected
through early this morning into today with rain rates as high as
0.2 inches per hour.
